rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, and nothing has been run yet, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing.

What this document declares, before anything has been run. "2 functions promise nothing" counts functions with no checks against them at all -- code the diagram is showing you but says nothing about. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.
`*` stands for every component
no component may call ingest.book — except ingest.decoder, strategy — such a call fails the build
`*` stands for every component
no component may call risk — except oms — such a call fails the build
`*` stands for every component
no component may call gateway — except oms — such a call fails the build

#8 marks an unresolved decision — a question the design still owes an answer: venue failover: mirror orders to a backup gateway or halt. It belongs to the workspace as a whole, not to any function or component yet; Ply tracks it until someone resolves it (§5.6).

component ingest — maps to Rust module ingest collapsed — 4 components and 7 functions folded inside; render with --depth or --focus <name> to expand no checks are declared anywhere in this component — nothing here is verified yet (unclaimed) this box is white because `feed.Feed::pump` declares no checks at all — one unchecked thing inside sets the shade of everything around it
this component may use `net` somewhere in its folded subtree. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).
this component may use `unsafe` somewhere in its folded subtree. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — using an undeclared one is an architecture finding (§5.3, A0404).

component strategy — maps to Rust module strat declares checks up to tested — checked once against the declared examples and generated inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `Strategy::on_update` is the weakest thing in it: it declares tested — checked once against the declared examples and generated inputs — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

component signals — maps to Rust module strat::signals pure — the double border is the seal: this component declares no capabilities and may not use any; capability use inside it is an error (A0408) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `momentum` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part
momentum bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times fuzz(2048) — runs the function on 2048 random inputs, checking the contract on each
Strategy::on_update test — runs the declared examples plus generated inputs, checking the contract on each

component risk — maps to Rust module risk owns risk::Limits — only this component may mutate them strict — architecture findings inside this component fail the build (errors, not warnings) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `check_order` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

check_order bounded(3) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 3 times fuzz(4096) — runs the function on 4096 random inputs, checking the contract on each mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; the test/fuzz checks must catch every one, or the contract is flagged weak contract at the watermark: requires: order.qty > 0 && order.px > 0 ensures: |r| r.is_err() == (order.qty > limits.max_qty) the checks above test the function against exactly this promise

Oms::submit bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times fuzz(256) — runs the function on 256 random inputs, checking the contract on each #9 marks an unresolved decision — a question this function still owes an answer: order id after venue reject: fresh id or reuse. strategy -> ingest.book — strategy may call ingest.book. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
strategy -> oms — strategy may call oms. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
oms -> risk — oms may call risk. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
oms -> gateway — oms may call gateway. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
oms -> pnl — oms may call pnl. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
BookUpdate data flows from ingest.book to strategy — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
OrderIntent data flows from strategy to oms — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
Order data flows from oms to gateway — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
Fill data flows from gateway to oms — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
Fill data flows from oms to pnl — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1
FixMessage data flows from gateway to venue — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1. venue is outside this codebase, so this arrow is a declaration, never a verified fact.
Fill data flows from venue to gateway — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1. venue is outside this codebase, so this arrow is a declaration, never a verified fact.
RawFrame data flows from venue to ingest.feed — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1. venue is outside this codebase, so this arrow is a declaration, never a verified fact.

entry — venue can reach Oms::submit from outside this codebase (declared via "entry: [venue]" on Oms::submit). no requires are declared on this function, so it makes no environmental assumption yet. Ply never checks this edge — it is declared, not verified.

venue — a system or person outside this codebase: the exchange: accepts orders, returns fills; market data source. Ply draws it so the boundary is visible, but checks nothing about it — every arrow touching it is a declaration, not a verified fact.
